what: Cleveland-Cliffs makes steel in the United States. It mines its own iron ore, pellets it, and runs blast furnaces and rolling mills producing flat-rolled steel, much of it the high-strength sheet that car makers stamp into body panels.
customers: Automobile manufacturers above all, plus appliance makers, construction product firms, pipe and tube producers and steel distributors.
money: Flat-rolled carbon steel, stainless and electrical steel, plus plate and tubular products.
Iron ore pellets sold externally and by-product revenue.
moat: It is vertically integrated from the iron ore mine to the finished coil, which no other North American steelmaker matches, and it is the largest supplier of automotive-grade sheet in the country. Automotive steel must be qualified for each vehicle programme, so supply relationships are long and hard to displace.
risks: The trailing twelve months show a net loss of about $473.0M and free cash flow of roughly negative $485.0M. The company is losing money and consuming cash.
Debt is about $7.5B against $57.0M of cash. With a $6.7B market value, the borrowings exceed the equity, which makes this a highly leveraged bet on steel prices.
Revenue has declined for four straight years, from $23.0B in 2022 to $18.6B in 2025.
Blast furnace steelmaking has higher fixed costs than the electric arc furnaces its competitors use, so downturns hurt it more.
Automotive production volumes and the steel price together determine results, and neither is under management control.
opportunities: Tariffs and trade policy on imported steel directly support domestic prices, and Cleveland-Cliffs is among the most exposed to that benefit.
The shares trade at about 0.33 times sales, which is what a market expecting losses pays.
Closing or idling the least efficient plants reduces the fixed cost base.
Ten analysts average a $14.75 target, about 26% above the current price, and the operating leverage in a steel recovery is extreme in both directions.
watch: The hot-rolled coil price. With debt exceeding the market value of the equity, this company's value is almost entirely a function of the steel price, and that one number drives the outcome.
